What the numbers say

In this revision 44 option-selling candidates across 16 underlyings passed the report's filters, all of them short puts. Expiries run from 4 to 64 days out with a median of 11.5 days; 9 of the 44 expire within seven days and 6 are more than 21 days out.

The highest composite score is 55.9 for the AMD 495 put expiring 2026-10-21 (6 days): premium $1.69, strike 10.1% below the share price, model probability of expiring out of the money 90.4%. Its displayed annualized yield of 20.8% multiplies a 6-day premium out to a full year, which is why the score discounts yields from contracts shorter than 30 days.

Implied volatility among the listed contracts is highest for MRVL (68.3%), NFLX (66.5%), TSLA (63.9%) and lowest for UNH (29.8%). High implied volatility is what makes a premium large; it is the market's price for a wide expected range, so the richest premiums sit on the names the market expects to move most.

Of the 27 underlyings with a quote, 15 were up and 12 down when the report was generated; the median move was +0.10%. Rising share prices move existing short puts further out of the money and shrink the premium available on new ones.

Against the previous session in this archive (2026-10-14), listed candidates went from 47 to 44 and the median time to expiry went from 16 to 11.5 days.

Backtest reference

The report carries a fixed reference backtest covering 2026-03-26 to 2026-04-22: 2,149 simulated option-selling trades with a 83.3% win rate and a profit factor of 0.70. A profit factor below 1 means total losses exceeded total gains even though most trades won. That is the characteristic risk of selling premium: many small wins and a few large losses. The window is short and does not include the session on this page; it is a description of that period, not an estimate of future results.
